SOVARA Technical Documentation

Reference material for the architecture, data models, security posture and operational behavior of SOVARA 1.1.4.

Download ArchitectureDownload Hardware MatrixDownload Release Verification

Architecture

Electron + React + AppBackend + local llama-server.

Storage

SQLite WAL + JSONL append-only audit log.

Model Lifecycle

Load → Active → Busy → Evict → Offline.

Hardware Validation

Detect → Profile → Estimate → Load → Infer → Measure → Validate.

Security

Sandbox + context isolation + Zod IPC + loopback inference.

Testing

101 automated tests.

ContentsOverviewArchitectureDesign DecisionsCore ComponentsData ModelsIntegrationsDeploymentPerformanceSecuritySovereigntyRenderer FeaturesHardware ProfilingTestingSetup & TroubleshootingOperational Runbook

Overview

SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4) that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference dependency and no telemetry.

The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64, combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.

Architecture

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

  • User
  • React Renderer
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
  • Main / AppBackend
  • Model / resource / tool ports
  • SQLite + JSONL
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1

Design Decisions

Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network conditions.

Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.

Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit trail.

Core Components

  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing

Data Models

Local persistence stores:

  • Sessions and projects
  • Messages
  • Token usage
  • Model registry
  • Routing / audit events
  • Settings

Structured metadata is stored in SQLite; execution history is appended to JSONL event logs.

Integrations

  • Hugging Face — model discovery for the Model Explorer
  • MCP — add, remove, toggle and probe connected tools/services
  • Automatic updates — stable and beta GitHub release channels
  • Web/Search infrastructure — supports select agent tool use

Deployment

SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally uses pnpm build:win. No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

Performance

SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization, and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.

The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.

Security

  • sandbox: true
  • contextIsolation: true
  • nodeIntegration: false
  • Content Security Policy
  • Navigation guards and window-open restrictions
  • Zod validation for IPC messages
  • Loopback-only inference networking

Sovereignty

Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.

Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.

Renderer Features

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

  • Chat with streaming responses
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
  • Connections — MCP server management

Hardware Profiling

SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

Testing

564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates, hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.

pnpm --filter @sovara/desktop testpnpm --filter @sovara/desktop typecheck

Setup & Troubleshooting

Requirements: Node >= 22, pnpm 11.17.0 for development. Users only need Windows x64 to run the packaged application.

  • git clone https://github.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA.git
  • pnpm install
  • pnpm dev

If GPU/VRAM profiling is unavailable, confirm an NVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi is installed — CPU-only operation remains supported without it.

Operational Runbook

On first run, SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline for local inference. Model downloads, MCP remote connections, and update checks are the explicit functions that use network access.

Automated test gates for sovereignty and security invariants run locally before packaging a release build.

npx --yes sovara@latest

\\r\\n \\r\\n

\\r\\n SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4)\\r\\n that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference\\r\\n dependency and no telemetry.\\r\\n

\\r\\n

\\r\\n The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64,\\r\\n combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local\\r\\n session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.\\r\\n

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

\\r\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\">\\r\\n
  • User
    • \\r\\n
  • React Renderer
    • \\r\\n
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
    • \\r\\n
  • Main / AppBackend
    • \\r\\n
  • Model / resource / tool ports
    • \\r\\n
  • SQLite + JSONL
    • \\r\\n
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1
    • \\r\\n
\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

\\r\\n Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote\\r\\n endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network\\r\\n conditions.\\r\\n

\\r\\n

\\r\\n Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every\\r\\n machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices\\r\\n accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.\\r\\n

\\r\\n

\\r\\n Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for\\r\\n event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit\\r\\n trail.\\r\\n

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\">\\r\\n
  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
    • \\r\\n
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
    • \\r\\n
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
    • \\r\\n
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
    • \\r\\n
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
    • \\r\\n
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing
    • \\r\\n
\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

Local persistence stores:

\\r\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\">\\r\\n
  • Sessions and projects
    • \\r\\n
  • Messages
    • \\r\\n
  • Token usage
    • \\r\\n
  • Model registry
    • \\r\\n
  • Routing / audit events
    • \\r\\n
  • Settings
    • \\r\\n
\\r\\n

\\r\\n Structured metadata is stored in SQLite; execution history is appended to JSONL\\r\\n event logs.\\r\\n

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\">\\r\\n
  • Hugging Face — model discovery for the Model Explorer
    • \\r\\n
  • MCP — add, remove, toggle and probe connected tools/services
    • \\r\\n
  • Automatic updates — stable and beta GitHub release channels
    • \\r\\n
  • Web/Search infrastructure — supports select agent tool use
    • \\r\\n
\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

\\r\\n SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally\\r\\n uses pnpm build:win.\\r\\n No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to\\r\\n the SOVARA data directory.\\r\\n

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

\\r\\n SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or\\r\\n guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization,\\r\\n and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.\\r\\n

\\r\\n

\\r\\n The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer →\\r\\n Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.\\r\\n

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\">\\r\\n
  • sandbox: true
    • \\r\\n
  • contextIsolation: true
    • \\r\\n
  • nodeIntegration: false
    • \\r\\n
  • Content Security Policy

\\r\\n Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.\\r\\n

\\r\\n

\\r\\n Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model\\r\\n discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not\\r\\n described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.\\r\\n

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

\\r\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\">\\r\\n
  • Chat with streaming responses
    • \\r\\n
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
    • \\r\\n
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
    • \\r\\n
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
    • \\r\\n
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
    • \\r\\n
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
    • \\r\\n
  • Connections — MCP server management
    • \\r\\n
\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

\\r\\n SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and\\r\\n quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not\\r\\n possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.\\r\\n

\\r\\n

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

\\r\\n \\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n

\\r\\n 564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model\\r\\n lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates,\\r\\n hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.\\r\\n

Overview

SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4) that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference dependency and no telemetry.

The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64, combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.

Architecture

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

  • User
  • React Renderer
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
  • Main / AppBackend
  • Model / resource / tool ports
  • SQLite + JSONL
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1

Design Decisions

Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network conditions.

Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.

Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit trail.

Core Components

  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing

Data Models

Local persistence stores:

  • Sessions and projects
  • Messages
  • Token usage
  • Model registry
  • Routing / audit events
  • Settings

Structured metadata is stored in SQLite; execution history is appended to JSONL event logs.

Integrations

  • Hugging Face — model discovery for the Model Explorer
  • MCP — add, remove, toggle and probe connected tools/services
  • Automatic updates — stable and beta GitHub release channels
  • Web/Search infrastructure — supports select agent tool use

Deployment

SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally uses pnpm build:win. No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

Performance

SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization, and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.

The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.

Security

  • sandbox: true
  • contextIsolation: true
  • nodeIntegration: false
  • Content Security Policy
  • Navigation guards and window-open restrictions
  • Zod validation for IPC messages
  • Loopback-only inference networking

Sovereignty

Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.

Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.

Renderer Features

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

  • Chat with streaming responses
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
  • Connections — MCP server management

Hardware Profiling

SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

Testing

564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates, hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.

pnpm --filter @sovara/desktop testpnpm --filter @sovara/desktop typecheck

Setup & Troubleshooting

Requirements: Node >= 22, pnpm 11.17.0 for development. Users only need Windows x64 to run the packaged application.

  • git clone https://github.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA.git
  • pnpm install
  • pnpm dev

If GPU/VRAM profiling is unavailable, confirm an NVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi is installed — CPU-only operation remains supported without it.

Operational Runbook

On first run, SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline for local inference. Model downloads, MCP remote connections, and update checks are the explicit functions that use network access.

Automated test gates for sovereignty and security invariants run locally before packaging a release build.

Fast Installation Alternatives

1-Line PowerShell Install:

iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA/main/install.ps1 | iex

Node.js / NPM Install:

npx --yes sovara@latest

Optional NVIDIA GPU improves local GPU inference and enables VRAM-aware profiling. CPU-only operation is supported.

For first-run runtime setup: SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline. Model downloads from Hugging Face require network access.

OSWindows 10 / 11 x64
CPUStandard modern Windows-compatible CPU

GPUOptional NVIDIA GPU
VRAMDepends on selected model / quantization

AdminNo admin privileges are required for normal use, except normal filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4)\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n dependency and no telemetry.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64,\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\">\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • User
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • React Renderer
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Main / AppBackend
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Model / resource / tool ports
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • SQLite + JSONL
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n conditions.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n trail.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\">\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n uses pnpm build:win.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n the SOVARA data directory.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization,\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer →\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Navigation guards and window-open restrictions
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
    li]:list-disc\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\">\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Chat with streaming responses
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
  • Connections — MCP server management
    • \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n
\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n 564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates,\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n

Overview

SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4) that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference dependency and no telemetry.

The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64, combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.

Architecture

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

  • User
  • React Renderer
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
  • Main / AppBackend
  • Model / resource / tool ports
  • SQLite + JSONL
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1

Design Decisions

Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network conditions.

Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.

Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit trail.

Core Components

  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing

Data Models

Local persistence stores:

  • Sessions and projects
  • Messages
  • Token usage
  • Model registry
  • Routing / audit events
  • Settings

Structured metadata is stored in SQLite; execution history is appended to JSONL event logs.

Integrations

  • Hugging Face — model discovery for the Model Explorer
  • MCP — add, remove, toggle and probe connected tools/services
  • Automatic updates — stable and beta GitHub release channels
  • Web/Search infrastructure — supports select agent tool use

Deployment

SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally uses pnpm build:win. No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

Performance

SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization, and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.

The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.

Security

  • sandbox: true
  • contextIsolation: true
  • nodeIntegration: false
  • Content Security Policy
  • Navigation guards and window-open restrictions
  • Zod validation for IPC messages
  • Loopback-only inference networking

Sovereignty

Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.

Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.

Renderer Features

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

  • Chat with streaming responses
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
  • Connections — MCP server management

Hardware Profiling

SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

Testing

564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates, hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.

pnpm --filter @sovara/desktop testpnpm --filter @sovara/desktop typecheck

Setup & Troubleshooting

Requirements: Node >= 22, pnpm 11.17.0 for development. Users only need Windows x64 to run the packaged application.

  • git clone https://github.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA.git
  • pnpm install
  • pnpm dev

If GPU/VRAM profiling is unavailable, confirm an NVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi is installed — CPU-only operation remains supported without it.

Operational Runbook

On first run, SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline for local inference. Model downloads, MCP remote connections, and update checks are the explicit functions that use network access.

Automated test gates for sovereignty and security invariants run locally before packaging a release build.

Getting Started

INSTALLATION GUIDE

1

Download the Windows .exe

Download the latest Sovara-Setup Windows .exe from the panel above.

2

Install / launch SOVARA

Run the installer, then launch the desktop workbench.

3

Select or download a local GGUF model

Choose an installed model or discover one through the Model Explorer.

Fast Installation Alternatives

1-Line PowerShell Install:

iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA/main/install.ps1 | iex

Node.js / NPM Install:

npx --yes sovara@latest

Optional NVIDIA GPU improves local GPU inference and enables VRAM-aware profiling. CPU-only operation is supported.

For first-run runtime setup: SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline. Model downloads from Hugging Face require network access.

Requirements

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

OSWindows 10 / 11 x64
CPUStandard modern Windows-compatible CPU
RAMRequired by the selected model
GPUOptional NVIDIA GPU
VRAMDepends on selected model / quantization
DriverNVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi for GPU/VRAM profiling
AdminNo admin privileges are required for normal use, except normal filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

Exact minimum RAM and VRAM values depend on the model and quantization you choose.

Documentation

SOVARA Technical Documentation

Reference material for the architecture, data models, security posture and operational behavior of SOVARA 1.1.4.

{/* mobile section nav */}
{docSections.map((section) => ( {section.label} ))}

SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4) that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference dependency and no telemetry.

The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64, combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

  • User
  • React Renderer
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
  • Main / AppBackend
  • Model / resource / tool ports
  • SQLite + JSONL
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1

Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network conditions.

Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.

Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit trail.

  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing

Local persistence stores:

  • Sessions and projects
  • Messages
  • Token usage
  • Model registry
  • Routing / audit events
  • Settings

Structured metadata is stored in SQLite; execution history is appended to JSONL event logs.

  • Hugging Face — model discovery for the Model Explorer
  • MCP — add, remove, toggle and probe connected tools/services
  • Automatic updates — stable and beta GitHub release channels
  • Web/Search infrastructure — supports select agent tool use

SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally uses pnpm build:win. No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization, and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.

The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.

  • sandbox: true
  • contextIsolation: true
  • nodeIntegration: false
  • Content Security Policy
  • Navigation guards and window-open restrictions
  • Zod validation for IPC messages
  • Loopback-only inference networking

Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.

Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

  • Chat with streaming responses
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
  • Connections — MCP server management

SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates, hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.

pnpm --filter @sovara/desktop test pnpm --filter @sovara/desktop typecheck

Requirements: Node >= 22, pnpm 11.17.0 for development. Users only need Windows x64 to run the packaged application.

  • git clone https://github.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA.git
  • pnpm install
  • pnpm dev

If GPU/VRAM profiling is unavailable, confirm an NVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi is installed — CPU-only operation remains supported without it.

On first run, SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline for local inference. Model downloads, MCP remote connections, and update checks are the explicit functions that use network access.

Automated test gates for sovereignty and security invariants run locally before packaging a release build.

Overview

SOVARA is a Windows desktop workbench (version 1.1.4) that runs GGUF models locally, offline by default, with no cloud inference dependency and no telemetry.

The application is distributed as an Electron .exe for Windows 10/11 x64, combining a hardened Chromium renderer, a Node.js main process, a durable local session store, and a bundled CUDA-capable llama.cpp runtime.

Architecture

The mental model for a request flowing through SOVARA:

  • User
  • React Renderer
  • Secure IPC using contextBridge + Zod
  • Main / AppBackend
  • Model / resource / tool ports
  • SQLite + JSONL
  • Local llama-server on 127.0.0.1

Design Decisions

Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network conditions.

Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.

Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit trail.

Core Components

  • AppBackend — coordinates ports, sessions and persistence
  • ChatService — manages chat sessions and streaming responses
  • AgentOrchestrator — task classification, routing, tool use, audit events
  • ModelWorkbench — model lifecycle: load, health check, evict
  • ModelRouter — considers capability and VRAM/resource constraints
  • TaskClassifier — identifies task type ahead of routing

Data Models

Local persistence stores:

  • Sessions and projects
  • Messages
  • Token usage
  • Model registry
  • Routing / audit events
  • Settings

Structured metadata is stored in SQLite; execution history is appended to JSONL event logs.

Integrations

  • Hugging Face — model discovery for the Model Explorer
  • MCP — add, remove, toggle and probe connected tools/services
  • Automatic updates — stable and beta GitHub release channels
  • Web/Search infrastructure — supports select agent tool use

Deployment

SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally uses pnpm build:win. No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

Performance

SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization, and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.

The hardware validation pipeline (Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure) is used to assess fit at runtime rather than rely on static claims.

Security

  • sandbox: true
  • contextIsolation: true
  • nodeIntegration: false
  • Content Security Policy
  • Navigation guards and window-open restrictions
  • Zod validation for IPC messages
  • Loopback-only inference networking

Sovereignty

Offline by default. No telemetry. No analytics SDK. No automatic cloud inference.

Network access is limited to explicit supported functions: Hugging Face model discovery/download, MCP remote connections, and update checks. SOVARA is not described as air-gapped, because these explicit functions may use the network.

Renderer Features

Built on React 18 + Vite, the renderer surfaces:

  • Chat with streaming responses
  • Models — lifecycle and compatibility status
  • Explore — Hugging Face model discovery
  • Library — download/pause/resume/cancel management
  • Agents — orchestration and tool permission control
  • Skills — scan, import and enable local skills
  • Connections — MCP server management

Hardware Profiling

SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.

Pipeline: Detect → Estimate → Validate → Load → Infer → Measure.

Testing

564 desktop tests cover sovereignty, security, IPC validation, persistence, model lifecycle, routing, agent orchestration, Explore, downloads, renderer, updates, hardware fit, and web/search infrastructure.

pnpm --filter @sovara/desktop testpnpm --filter @sovara/desktop typecheck

Setup & Troubleshooting

Requirements: Node >= 22, pnpm 11.17.0 for development. Users only need Windows x64 to run the packaged application.

  • git clone https://github.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA.git
  • pnpm install
  • pnpm dev

If GPU/VRAM profiling is unavailable, confirm an NVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi is installed — CPU-only operation remains supported without it.

Operational Runbook

On first run, SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline for local inference. Model downloads, MCP remote connections, and update checks are the explicit functions that use network access.

Automated test gates for sovereignty and security invariants run locally before packaging a release build.

Getting Started

INSTALLATION GUIDE

1

Download the Windows .exe

Download the latest Sovara-Setup Windows .exe from the panel above.

2

Install / launch SOVARA

Run the installer, then launch the desktop workbench.

3

Select or download a local GGUF model

Choose an installed model or discover one through the Model Explorer.

Fast Installation Alternatives

1-Line PowerShell Install:

iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthik-ak-Git/SOVARA/main/install.ps1 | iex

Node.js / NPM Install:

npx --yes sovara@latest

Optional NVIDIA GPU improves local GPU inference and enables VRAM-aware profiling. CPU-only operation is supported.

For first-run runtime setup: SOVARA may provision its pinned local llama.cpp runtime once, then operate offline. Model downloads from Hugging Face require network access.

Requirements

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

OSWindows 10 / 11 x64
CPUStandard modern Windows-compatible CPU
RAMRequired by the selected model
GPUOptional NVIDIA GPU
VRAMDepends on selected model / quantization
DriverNVIDIA driver with nvidia-smi for GPU/VRAM profiling
AdminNo admin privileges are required for normal use, except normal filesystem write access to the SOVARA data directory.

Exact minimum RAM and VRAM values depend on the model and quantization you choose.

\\\\r\\\\n \\\\r\\\\n\\\\r\\\\n \\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n Inference is kept on loopback networking (127.0.0.1) rather than a remote\\\\r\\\\n endpoint, so model execution does not depend on cloud availability or network\\\\r\\\\n conditions.\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n Hardware-aware routing exists because a single fixed model cannot fit every\\\\r\\\\n machine — SOVARA profiles the host and adjusts model and quantization choices\\\\r\\\\n accordingly, with LRU-based eviction to reclaim memory under pressure.\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n Persistence uses SQLite for structured metadata alongside append-only JSONL for\\\\r\\\\n event history, giving both queryable state and a durable, tamper-evident audit\\\\r\\\\n trail.\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n SOVARA is packaged as a Windows .exe (Sovara-Setup-1.1.4-x64.exe). Building locally\\\\r\\\\n uses pnpm build:win.\\\\r\\\\n No admin privileges are required for normal use beyond filesystem write access to\\\\r\\\\n the SOVARA data directory.\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n SOVARA does not publish fixed benchmark numbers, token-per-second figures, or\\\\r\\\\n guaranteed throughput. Performance depends on the selected model, quantization,\\\\r\\\\n and the host's CPU/GPU/VRAM.\\\\r\\\\n

\\\\r\\\\n SOVARA detects CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM, then estimates whether a given model and\\\\r\\\\n quantization are likely to fit before loading. When a full GPU fit is not\\\\r\\\\n possible, SOVARA can fall back to a partial fit or CPU execution.\\\\r\\\\n

{"name":"arena","source":"Bionic","content":"---
name: arena
description: >-
  Make 100 versions of Claude fight to the death over one task. Spins up N
  sub-agents (default 100, --quick for 16), gives every one the exact same
  task plus a different strategy card (reasoning mode, workflow, strategy),
  then runs a single-elimination bracket: they attack each other's solutions,
  defend and revise, and a judge scores every match on a written rubric until
  one solution survives. Use when the user is not satisfied with an answer,
  calls it a bad answer, says try again or do better, says "arena", or asks
  to make them compete.
argument-hint: "[--agents N | --quick] [--seed S] <task>"
---

# arena

For when Claude keeps giving a bad answer. Instead of asking again and again, this runs a tournament:
N sub-agents get the exact same task, each attacks it with a different reasoning mode, workflow and
strategy, and then they attack each other in a bracket until one solution is left. You are the
orchestrator. You never compete and you never judge.

What the user typed after `/arena`: `$ARGUMENTS`

If that is blank, or still reads like a placeholder, nothing was passed: take the task from the
conversation.

## The tool

Every piece of bookkeeping goes through `bracket.py` in this skill's folder:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/bracket.py" <command>
```

Below, `ARENA` means exactly that command. If the path looks unexpanded, use the "Base directory for
this skill" that Claude Code printed at the top of this skill. The state lives in
`.arena/<run>/arena.json` in the current directory, and every command after `init` finds it through
`.arena/LATEST`.

## Step 1: size it, and get a yes if nobody asked for it

Read the flags out of the request. Everything that is not a flag is the task.

| flag | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--agents N` | N competitors. Default 100. |
| `--quick` | 16 competitors. The everyday setting. |
| `--seed S` | Fixes the cards and the pairings. Default: random, and recorded. |
| `--wave W` | Sub-agents per wave. Default 10. Only raise it if the user raised Claude Code's limit. |

No task text at all means: the task is the user's most recent request in this conversation, and your
last answer to it is the baseline to beat.

Run `ARENA plan --agents N` (or `--quick`). It prints the rounds, the sub-agent calls and the waves.

- **The user asked for the arena** (typed `/arena`, said "arena", or asked to make them compete):
  tell them in one line how big it is, for example "100 agents, 7 rounds, 595 sub-agent calls", and
  start.
- **This skill fired because the user is unhappy** ("that's wrong", "try again", "bad answer") and
  never mentioned the arena: ask once before spending anything. Offer three options: the full arena
  (100 agents, 595 sub-agent calls), `--quick` (16 agents, 91 calls), or an ordinary retry. Wait for
  the answer.

Sub-agents write their work into `.arena/` in the current directory. In the default permission mode
that is one approval per file, which is hundreds on a big run. Before the spawn phase, suggest
accept-edits mode (Shift+Tab) for the run. Do not change the user's settings yourself.

## Step 2: write the task file

This is the step that decides the result. **Sub-agents cannot see this conversation.** Every
competitor, attacker and judge knows only what is in the task file, so write `.arena/task.md` to stand
on its own:

- The request, in the user's own words where you can.
- Every requirement and constraint the user stated anywhere in the conversation: audience, length,
  format, tone, stack, deadline, what must not change.
- The context a stranger would need: absolute paths of the files that matter, pasted data, what the
  product is, the conventions in the codebase.
- What "done" looks like, if the user said.
- If there is an answer to beat: what the user disliked about it, in their words.

Do not add requirements the user never gave. Do not write your own view of the right answer into it:
that pushes 100 agents the same way, which is the opposite of the point.

If there is an earlier answer the user was not satisfied with, write it word for word to
`.arena/baseline.md`.

## Step 3: init

```bash
ARENA init --agents N --seed S --task-file .arena/task.md --baseline-file .arena/baseline.md
```

Leave out `--baseline-file` when there is nothing to beat, and `--seed` to get a random one. `init`
copies the task into the run folder, deals every competitor a different strategy card with no
repeats, pairs round 1, and writes `arena.json`.

## Step 4: the loop

Always drive it with `ARENA next`. It reads the state on disk and tells you the next step and the
exact command.

Every phase that runs sub-agents works the same way:

1. `ARENA prompts <phase>` writes one brief per job and lists the jobs still to run, in waves.
2. Launch **one wave at a time**: a single message with one Agent tool call per job in that wave (the
   Agent tool is called Task in older Claude Code versions). Each call is:
   - `subagent_type`: `general-purpose`
   - `description`: `arena <job id>`
   - `prompt`: `Read <prompt path> and follow it exactly. It is your whole brief.`
   - `run_in_background`: false, where the tool has that option, so the wave comes back together.

   Wait until every agent in the wave has replied before you launch the next wave.
3. After the last wave, run `ARENA next`. If an output is missing it sends you back to the same
   phase, and `prompts` then lists only the missing jobs. Re-run those once. If a job fails twice,
   write the single line `NO OUTPUT` into each of its output files (`ARENA check <phase>` lists
   them) and move on. A missing attack counts as no attacks. A missing solution loses its match. A
   judge that fails twice gets a third, fresh run: never decide a match yourself.

The order `next` takes you through:

- **spawn**, once: every competitor writes its own solution to the task.
- then every round: **attack** (two per match) → **defend** (two per match) → **judge** (one per
  match) → `ARENA collect` → `ARENA advance`.
- **final**, once, only when there is a baseline: a judge compares the champion with the answer the
  user rejected, blind to which is which. Then `ARENA collect`.
- `next` prints DONE: go to step 5.

After each `advance`, give the user one line, such as "Round 2 done: 25 of 100 left." Nothing more.
Never paste pairings, attacks, verdicts or solutions into the chat.

Why waves: Claude Code runs at most 10 tool calls at once by default (the
`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY` setting). So a 100-agent spawn is 10 waves of 10, and a
100-agent arena is 70 waves in total, 71 with the final check.

## Step 5: the result

Run `ARENA winner`, then read the champion's solution file at the path it prints. That is the only
solution file you read in the whole run. Give the user:

1. **The winning solution**, in full.
2. **Why it won**: the attacks it survived, from `winner`, as a short list. Its card on one line
   (reasoning mode + workflow + strategy).
3. **Rounds**: for example "7 rounds, 100 agents in, 1 left."
4. **Against the answer you rejected**, if there was one: the final check's scores, honestly. If the
   old answer scored higher, say so plainly and show both.
5. Where the full record lives: the run folder.

If the solution changes files in the user's project, do not apply it. Ask: apply it, or change it?

## Rules for the orchestrator

- You run the tournament. You do not compete, attack or judge, and you never pick a winner.
  `collect` records what the judges decided. `record` is only for fixing bookkeeping when the user
  asks you to.
- Every sub-agent gets the task through its brief, which `prompts` builds from the one task file,
  byte for byte the same for everyone. Never paraphrase the task for one agent or add a hint to one
  agent's call.
- Do not read solutions, attacks or verdicts during the run. There are hundreds of them. The state
  is on disk, and `next`, `status` and `pairings` are all you need.
- If your context gets compacted mid-run, nothing is lost. Run `ARENA status`, then `ARENA next`,
  and carry on.
- Run every `ARENA` command from the directory you ran `init` in. That is where `.arena/LATEST`
  lives.
- Sub-agents only write inside `.arena/`. If one wrote anywhere else, tell the user.
- If the user says stop, stop. `ARENA status` shows where it got to, and `ARENA next` resumes it
  later.

## The prompt templates

`bracket.py` fills these in (the `{{placeholders}}`) and writes one brief per job, so what you see
here is exactly what every sub-agent is told. Never edit a brief for a single agent.

### Competitor, in the spawn phase

<!-- template:competitor -->
```text
You are competitor {{agent}} in an arena of {{n}}. All {{n}} competitors got the exact same task, word for word. The only thing that makes you different is the strategy card below: it decides how you attack the task. Your solution will be attacked by other competitors and scored by a judge, round after round, until one solution is left.

=== THE TASK (identical for every competitor) ===
{{task}}
=== END OF THE TASK ===

---
name: arena
description: >-
  Make 100 versions of Claude fight to the death over one task. Spins up N
  sub-agents (default 100, --quick for 16), gives every one the exact same
  task plus a different strategy card (reasoning mode, workflow, strategy),
  then runs a single-elimination bracket: they attack each other's solutions,
  defend and revise, and a judge scores every match on a written rubric until
  one solution survives. Use when the user is not satisfied with an answer,
  calls it a bad answer, says try again or do better, says "arena", or asks
  to make them compete.
argument-hint: "[--agents N | --quick] [--seed S] <task>"
---

# arena

For when Claude keeps giving a bad answer. Instead of asking again and again, this runs a tournament:
N sub-agents get the exact same task, each attacks it with a different reasoning mode, workflow and
strategy, and then they attack each other in a bracket until one solution is left. You are the
orchestrator. You never compete and you never judge.

What the user typed after `/arena`: `$ARGUMENTS`

If that is blank, or still reads like a placeholder, nothing was passed: take the task from the
conversation.

## The tool

Every piece of bookkeeping goes through `bracket.py` in this skill's folder:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/bracket.py" <command>
```

Below, `ARENA` means exactly that command. If the path looks unexpanded, use the "Base directory for
this skill" that Claude Code printed at the top of this skill. The state lives in
`.arena/<run>/arena.json` in the current directory, and every command after `init` finds it through
`.arena/LATEST`.

## Step 1: size it, and get a yes if nobody asked for it

Read the flags out of the request. Everything that is not a flag is the task.

| flag | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--agents N` | N competitors. Default 100. |
| `--quick` | 16 competitors. The everyday setting. |
| `--seed S` | Fixes the cards and the pairings. Default: random, and recorded. |
| `--wave W` | Sub-agents per wave. Default 10. Only raise it if the user raised Claude Code's limit. |

No task text at all means: the task is the user's most recent request in this conversation, and your
last answer to it is the baseline to beat.

Run `ARENA plan --agents N` (or `--quick`). It prints the rounds, the sub-agent calls and the waves.

- **The user asked for the arena** (typed `/arena`, said "arena", or asked to make them compete):
  tell them in one line how big it is, for example "100 agents, 7 rounds, 595 sub-agent calls", and
  start.
- **This skill fired because the user is unhappy** ("that's wrong", "try again", "bad answer") and
  never mentioned the arena: ask once before spending anything. Offer three options: the full arena
  (100 agents, 595 sub-agent calls), `--quick` (16 agents, 91 calls), or an ordinary retry. Wait for
  the answer.

Sub-agents write their work into `.arena/` in the current directory. In the default permission mode
that is one approval per file, which is hundreds on a big run. Before the spawn phase, suggest
accept-edits mode (Shift+Tab) for the run. Do not change the user's settings yourself.

## Step 2: write the task file

This is the step that decides the result. **Sub-agents cannot see this conversation.** Every
competitor, attacker and judge knows only what is in the task file, so write `.arena/task.md` to stand
on its own:

- The request, in the user's own words where you can.
- Every requirement and constraint the user stated anywhere in the conversation: audience, length,
  format, tone, stack, deadline, what must not change.
- The context a stranger would need: absolute paths of the files that matter, pasted data, what the
  product is, the conventions in the codebase.
- What "done" looks like, if the user said.
- If there is an answer to beat: what the user disliked about it, in their words.

Do not add requirements the user never gave. Do not write your own view of the right answer into it:
that pushes 100 agents the same way, which is the opposite of the point.

If there is an earlier answer the user was not satisfied with, write it word for word to
`.arena/baseline.md`.

## Step 3: init

```bash
ARENA init --agents N --seed S --task-file .arena/task.md --baseline-file .arena/baseline.md
```

Leave out `--baseline-file` when there is nothing to beat, and `--seed` to get a random one. `init`
copies the task into the run folder, deals every competitor a different strategy card with no
repeats, pairs round 1, and writes `arena.json`.

## Step 4: the loop

Always drive it with `ARENA next`. It reads the state on disk and tells you the next step and the
exact command.

Every phase that runs sub-agents works the same way:

1. `ARENA prompts <phase>` writes one brief per job and lists the jobs still to run, in waves.
2. Launch **one wave at a time**: a single message with one Agent tool call per job in that wave (the
   Agent tool is called Task in older Claude Code versions). Each call is:
   - `subagent_type`: `general-purpose`
   - `description`: `arena <job id>`
   - `prompt`: `Read <prompt path> and follow it exactly. It is your whole brief.`
   - `run_in_background`: false, where the tool has that option, so the wave comes back together.

   Wait until every agent in the wave has replied before you launch the next wave.
3. After the last wave, run `ARENA next`. If an output is missing it sends you back to the same
   phase, and `prompts` then lists only the missing jobs. Re-run those once. If a job fails twice,
   write the single line `NO OUTPUT` into each of its output files (`ARENA check <phase>` lists
   them) and move on. A missing attack counts as no attacks. A missing solution loses its match. A
   judge that fails twice gets a third, fresh run: never decide a match yourself.

The order `next` takes you through:

- **spawn**, once: every competitor writes its own solution to the task.
- then every round: **attack** (two per match) → **defend** (two per match) → **judge** (one per
  match) → `ARENA collect` → `ARENA advance`.
- **final**, once, only when there is a baseline: a judge compares the champion with the answer the
  user rejected, blind to which is which. Then `ARENA collect`.
- `next` prints DONE: go to step 5.

After each `advance`, give the user one line, such as "Round 2 done: 25 of 100 left." Nothing more.
Never paste pairings, attacks, verdicts or solutions into the chat.

Why waves: Claude Code runs at most 10 tool calls at once by default (the
`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY` setting). So a 100-agent spawn is 10 waves of 10, and a
100-agent arena is 70 waves in total, 71 with the final check.

## Step 5: the result

Run `ARENA winner`, then read the champion's solution file at the path it prints. That is the only
solution file you read in the whole run. Give the user:

1. **The winning solution**, in full.
2. **Why it won**: the attacks it survived, from `winner`, as a short list. Its card on one line
   (reasoning mode + workflow + strategy).
3. **Rounds**: for example "7 rounds, 100 agents in, 1 left."
4. **Against the answer you rejected**, if there was one: the final check's scores, honestly. If the
   old answer scored higher, say so plainly and show both.
5. Where the full record lives: the run folder.

If the solution changes files in the user's project, do not apply it. Ask: apply it, or change it?

## Rules for the orchestrator

- You run the tournament. You do not compete, attack or judge, and you never pick a winner.
  `collect` records what the judges decided. `record` is only for fixing bookkeeping when the user
  asks you to.
- Every sub-agent gets the task through its brief, which `prompts` builds from the one task file,
  byte for byte the same for everyone. Never paraphrase the task for one agent or add a hint to one
  agent's call.
- Do not read solutions, attacks or verdicts during the run. There are hundreds of them. The state
  is on disk, and `next`, `status` and `pairings` are all you need.
- If your context gets compacted mid-run, nothing is lost. Run `ARENA status`, then `ARENA next`,
  and carry on.
- Run every `ARENA` command from the directory you ran `init` in. That is where `.arena/LATEST`
  lives.
- Sub-agents only write inside `.arena/`. If one wrote anywhere else, tell the user.
- If the user says stop, stop. `ARENA status` shows where it got to, and `ARENA next` resumes it
  later.

## The prompt templates

`bracket.py` fills these in (the `{{placeholders}}`) and writes one brief per job, so what you see
here is exactly what every sub-agent is told. Never edit a brief for a single agent.

### Competitor, in the spawn phase

<!-- template:competitor -->
```text
You are competitor {{agent}} in an arena of {{n}}. All {{n}} competitors got the exact same task, word for word. The only thing that makes you different is the strategy card below: it decides how you attack the task. Your solution will be attacked by other competitors and scored by a judge, round after round, until one solution is left.

=== THE TASK (identical for every competitor) ===
{{task}}
=== END OF THE TASK ===

{{baseline_note}}

=== YOUR STRATEGY CARD ===
Reasoning mode: {{reasoning_name}}. {{reasoning_how}}
Workflow: {{workflow_name}}. {{workflow_how}}
Strategy: {{strategy_name}}. {{strategy_how}}
=== END OF THE CARD ===

How to work:
1. Use the card for real. Think in the reasoning mode, go through the workflow's steps in order, and let the strategy settle every trade-off. A generic answer with the card's name on top will lose.
2. Meet every requirement the task states. The judge scores you against the task, not against your card.
3. You cannot ask the user anything. Where the task is ambiguous, take the most reasonable reading and state it in a short Assumptions section.
4. Expect attac
